REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 27, 2020 -
07:00 P.M.
TELECONFERENCE MEETING AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20 VIA ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID #811 6514 2925
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, the City Council Chamber and City Hall are closed to the public. Consistent with State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the Los Angeles County Health Officer’s “Safer at Home Order for Control of COVID-19” the City Council will participate in the meeting through teleconference. Public participation in the meeting will be facilitated through the electronic methods as described below.
Agenda Materials:
The agenda and agenda packet related to items on this agenda are available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet will be made available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION:
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us and on Cerritos TV3.
Public Comments:
Members of the public may provide public comment through the following methods:
Email: Members of the public may provide public comment by submitting an email to city_clerk@cerritos.us by 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the meeting date and agenda item number for which you would like to provide comment in the subject line of the email. The public comment will be distributed to all members of the City Council. During the meeting your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: You may provide audio public comment by connecting to the teleconference meeting online or by telephone/mobile call (please select only one method). Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time on the agenda. You must be available to provide comment at the time you are called upon to speak. If you are not planning on providing public comment we encourage you to observe the meeting via livestream or on Cerritos TV3 to allow staff to more effectively manage the number of teleconference connections.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81165142925
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 811 6514 2925
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations:
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
THURSDAY, AUGUST 27, 2020, 7:00 P.M., TELECONFERENCED MEETING AUTHORIZED
BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM
VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 811 6514 2925

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council as follows:

  National Women’s Suffrage Month (in honor of the 100th Anniversary of the 19th
  Amendment).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Erik Berg spoke in opposition to Cerritos athletic facility closures related to the COVID-
  19 local emergency.

  Matthew Ellis spoke regarding street lighting maintenance issues along Bloomfield
  Avenue and 183rd Street and on Towne Center Drive.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August 13,
  2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  August 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August 13, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 27, 2020
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of
  Demands, as follows:

  City of Cerritos  8/27/2020  $ 5,643,116.45 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated August 27, 2020 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of
  Demands, as follows:

  Successor Agency  8/27/2020  $ 2,862.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for professional design services for the roof replacement at the
  Cerritos City Hall, Project No. 12704, RFP No. 1404-20 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Award a contract for professional design services in the amount of $40,000.00 for the
  roof replacement at the Cerritos City Hall, Project No. 12704, RFP No. 1404-20, to BEAM
  Professionals and reject the other proposal; and
 City of Cerritos  August 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract modifications that
  may be necessary to complete the specified scope of work (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of contract for the repair and maintenance of the holiday decorations to be
  funded through the Art in Public Places Trust Fund (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration by
  Councilmember Yokoyama.

  Staff reports were given by Art Gallucci, City Manager, and Kanna Vancheswaran,
  Director Public Works/Water & Power. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Approve the appropriation and expenditures of $67,625.00 from the Art in Public Places
  Trust Fund for the repair and maintenance of the holiday decorations; and

  2. Authorize the award of a contract in the amount of $32,625.00 to Pacific Rim Resources
  for the holiday decorations refurbishment work for an initial term of one (1) year with a
  provision to extend for up to three (3) one-year extensions; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute any change orders necessary to complete the
  project (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Barrows
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency and report from County of Los Angeles Department of Public
  Health (COUNCIL).

  A brief staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City & Theater Marketing Manager/City
  Librarian. Ms. Noel Barakat, RN, MSN, MPH, Regional Health Officer, County of Los
  Angeles Public Health Department, provided a report regarding the County’s COVID-19
  pandemic response and provided various data related to COVID-19 impacts in Cerritos.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  August 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Pursuant to public notice regarding this
  item, the representative from the County Department of Public Health responded to
  written and audio inquiries from members of the public.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Tobi Balma submitted written correspondence inquiring about specific information
  related to City of Cerritos demographics of positive COVID-19 cases and deaths.

  Omar Med submitted written correspondence inquiring about the State of California’s
  contingency plans in the event of a continued increase in positive cases of COVID-19.

  Audio public comments

  Daisy Legasca inquired whether the County Department of Public Health COVID-19
  prevention recommendations are based upon Center for Disease Control (CDC) or World
  Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. She also inquired how the case numbers are
  documented based upon location of testing, home residence, and other hospital care
  facilities.

  Tobi Balma inquired whether the County Health Department representative could
  reinforce the face covering requirements as recommended by the County, particularly
  when the individual is exercising outside alone.

  A public speaker (telephone number ending in “928”) inquired as to the cost or
  insurance requirements for COVID-19 testing at County facilities.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

9B.  Review and consideration of a request by CalMet Services for an extraordinary
  adjustment to the maximum allowable solid waste management rates (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Mike O’Grady, Environmental Services Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Billie Szumiak and RFSLAC submitted written correspondence inquiring about the details
  of Calmet Services’ contract with the City.

  Sue Carter submitted written correspondence expressing concern with a Councilmember
  posting their stance on this item on social media.
 City of Cerritos  August 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  The following individuals submitted written correspondence in opposition to a CalMet
  Services rate increase: Peggy Paddock, Lifei Cheng, Rusty Chiang, Nancy Pang, Jimmy
  Mak, Cheng-Ai Tan, Jialung Yu, Brian Chu, Agarwals, Mott Surasmith, Sharon Yuan,
  Reggie Bauwens, Emily Chen-Darnell, MeiYing Huang, Leanna Culton, and Kimberly
  Thompson.

  The following individuals submitted written correspondence in support of a CalMet
  Services rate increase: Sumi Patel, Greg Knapp, Barbara Cusick, Innie Choi, Sue Carter,
  Irene Brown, Alan Tao, Lucy Dannecker, Ed Kamiyama, Tiffany Mitchell, Brandon Joe,
  Mark Kuramoto, Bryan Dilbeck, and Eddie Salcedo.

  Audio public comments

  Jay Gray expressed concerns with the process related to negotiating the 10-year
  contract with CalMet Services and previous contractual agreements with the service
  provider.

  Mel Cortez expressed concerns with the process related to negotiating the 10-year
  contract with CalMet Services and expressed interest in the City going out to bid to find
  a lower cost service provider.

  Daisy Legasca spoke in opposition to the proposed rate adjustment request by CalMet
  Services citing the financial impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.

  Tobi Balma spoke in opposition to the proposed rate adjustment request by CalMet
  Services and requested the City Council table this item to a future date.

  D. Seman spoke in support of City Council approval of the proposed rate adjustment
  request by CalMet Services citing the need for the City to act in good faith with regard to
  an approved contract.

  Murali Vasudevan stated he did not oppose the proposed rate adjustment request by
  CalMet Services although would prefer the City go out to bid for future contracts.

  Mark Shin spoke in support of City Council approval of the proposed rate adjustment
  request by CalMet Services and inquired regarding how the service provider would be
  handling upcoming state regulatory requirements regarding organics.

  Councilmember Yokoyama stated he submitted written correspondence related to this
  item on Thursday, August 27, 2020 to the Office of the City Clerk. The City Clerk
  confirmed any written correspondence submitted subsequent to the stated 3:00 p.m.
  deadline was available in the Office of the City Clerk as public record. (Written
  correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted written
  correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION DID NOT PASS DUE TO LACK OF A SECOND: A motion made by Barrows to
  reduce the proposed increase to the residential rates and suspend the 5% CalMet
  Services residential franchise fee did not pass due to the lack of a second (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  August 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to approve CalMet
  Services’ request to adjust the maximum allowable solid waste management rates in
  Cerritos by the following amounts effective September 1, 2020:

  Residential:  16.0% increase
  Commercial Bin:  13.7% increase
  Commercial Roll-Off:  18.0% increase

  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Hu, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of designation of a Voting Delegate and Alternates for the
  2020 League of California Cities Annual Conference and Business Meeting scheduled for
  October 7 - 9, 2020 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Designate Councilmember Hu, as Voting Delegate, and Councilmember Yokoyama,
  as Voting Alternate, as officially authorized to cast the City’s vote at the 2020
  League of California Cities Annual Business Meeting currently scheduled for Friday,
  October 9, 2020; and

  2. Direct the City Clerk to complete the official 2020 Annual Conference Voting
  Delegate/Alternate Form (Form), including attestation of the City Council’s majority
  action to designate a Voting Delegate and Alternate, and submit such Form to the
  League Credentials Committee by the August 31, 2020 advised deadline (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.
 City of Cerritos  August 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 7

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmember Yokoyama and Mayor Pro Tem Vo.

  MOTION DID NOT PASS DUE TO LACK OF A SECOND: A motion made by Yokoyama,
  citing the need for residents to be aware of the expenditure of taxpayer funds, that the
  proposal to spend City funds on magnetic car signs for the Cerritos City Councilmembers as
  an additional benefit to the City Councilmembers be placed as an agenda item at a future
  meeting for consideration did not pass due to lack of a second (COUNCIL).

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session to discuss the items listed on the
  Closed Session agenda.

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Manager

12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Clerk/Treasurer

12D. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6 (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Art Gallucci, Patricia Leyva, and Charles Goldstein
  Employee Organization: AFSCME, Local 619

12E.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6 (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Art Gallucci and Charles Goldstein
  Unrepresented Employees: Full-Time Exempt

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:46 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
